Issued at 409 AM CDT Tue Oct 27 2026

Presently, a weak surface cyclone is situated over the NE/IA border, 
with an attendant stationary front draped to the southwest towards 
Salina. Weak synoptic ascent from a broad LLJ and moist flow over 
the boundary is leading to light rain showers within the vicinity of 
the boundary early this morning, intersecting far NW MO. RAP 
sounding analyses show that this area still contains a stout layer 
of dry air near the surface, so this narrow corridor of 
precipitation will really need to work to moisten the near surface 
layer before drizzle/light rain can manifest for these areas. Else, 
chances of precipitation will gradually subside after sunrise as the 
greater synoptic forcing from the surface low and passing shortwave 
lifts off towards the northeast. Any momentum transfer towards the 
surface from virga with passing showers will provide brief 
opportunities for some localized gusts through the early morning.

At the larger scale, several shortwave disturbances are traversing 
the periphery of synoptic ridging, which is broadly situated over 
the eastern third of the CONUS. WV imagery shows a dense field of 
cloud cover just upstream of KS/MO, which will lower overall solar 
radiation during the daytime and help bring highs down to the low 
70s across much of the forecast area. A developing shortwave off the 
Rockies will enhance low-level WAA and broad synoptic ascent from a 
strengthening LLJ, boosting additional low-end chances (10-20%) for 
precipitation overnight tonight into tomorrow morning. The greatest 
chances reside over eastern KS/western MO with this activity, 
following the thermal ridge axis and the nose of the LLJ. As the 
shortwave lifts along the periphery of the ridge to the northeast, 
enhanced low-level WAA from strong south/southwesterly winds will 
help temperatures rise back into the high 70s/low 80s across the 
forecast area during the daytime. Additional moist advection along 
this corridor will bring dewpoints to the low 60s. This will enhance 
instability in advance of a cold frontal boundary draping 
southeastward from the retreating surface low by Wednesday evening, 
with MUCAPE residing around 1500 J/kg for portions of NW MO/NE KS. 
With the primary forcing for ascent coming from the cold frontal 
boundary, and building inhibition in advance of the front through 
the evening, more factors are looking to work against the 
probability of surface-based severe activity during this timeframe. 
If showers/storms do initiate, they look to remain elevated through 
the overnight period, with primary hazards of strong wind and hail 
earlier in the period from steepening lapse rates out ahead of the 
cold front. However, overall severe expectations continue to remain 
lower with this activity.

As the cold front sags to the south, chances (15-30%) for 
precipitation continue along that boundary through Thursday. 
However, with a lack of significant synoptic forcing out ahead of 
the boundary, chances will look to decrease during the daytime. 
Temperatures behind the front cool back down to the low 70s, with 
areas out ahead of the front remaining warmer in the high 70s/low 
80s. Of course, with the prospect of any front that moves over our 
forecast area, there could be some variation still in where exactly 
temperatures will cool versus stay warm during the day Thursday. An 
additional caveat will be the presence of any precipitation, as that 
will additionally influence temperatures during the daytime. As of 
right now, some signal in temperature spread exists around the US-
36/I-70 corridors through the LREF and NBM (~4-6 degF spread), 
indicating there is some variability in current guidance that could 
be better resolved in the coming days. For those of us who are 
dreading the prospect of continued high temperatures in the 80s as 
we approach the start of November, fear not! Your time for cooler 
temperatures looks to come soon...

Weak ascent and WAA over the boundary will increase precipitation 
chances (40-60%) yet again late Thursday/Friday, primarily 
across northern MO. An upper trough lifting from the southern 
Plains will keep precipitation chances around Friday into 
Saturday, with temperatures trending down to the high 60s/low 
70s by the start of the weekend. Increasing model divergence by
the weekend leaves some details a bit fuzzy at this time, but 
greater agreement exists on weather drying out by late weekend 
with a brief bout of amplified ridging at the synoptic level 
before a deep trough pushes eastward by early next week, 
increasing PoPs to close out the forecast period. Temperatures
remain on the cooler side to close out the forecast period with
increased precipitation chances.
